subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should the repository trust and adopt these 14 new action revisions across the secret-bearing and repository-mutating workflows after a current-main rebase?
rationale: The patch is mechanically correct, but selecting executable third-party revisions for privileged workflows is a supply-chain ownership decision that CI and automated review cannot safely make.

options.title: Rebase, validate, and approve
options.body: Refresh the branch, audit the upstream revisions, exercise representative privileged workflows, and merge only after the exact head passes.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Separate Codex, release, token-minting, and repository-mutation actions from lower-risk toolchain updates for narrower review and rollback.

options.title: Pause the grouped update
options.body: Leave current pins in place until Dependabot can refresh the branch or owners can validate each high-risk action family independently.

recommendation.title: Rebase, validate, and approve
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, audit the upstream revisions, exercise representative privileged workflows, and merge only after the exact head passes.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available repository and release-workflow owner signal for approving cross-workflow supply-chain changes.
